title: Searching logs without a large bill
summary: Give a small team fast answers from their logs for a fraction of what a hosted tool would cost.
context: Bisibele Foods runs about 40 services and writes around 200 GB of logs a day. Their hosted tool's bill has passed their whole database bill, so they turned off most logging, and the last outage took three hours to understand.
Most searches look at the last hour, for a request id or an error. An audit asks about something from months ago perhaps twice a year.
must_handle: A search for one request id over the last day returns within seconds.
Logs from a crashing service are not lost.
Secrets and customer details must not end up searchable.
Old logs get cheaper to keep and remain reachable for a year.
A noisy service cannot push out everyone else's logs.
show_in_answer: How a log line travels from a service to where it can be searched.
How data moves between storage tiers, and what a search does across them.
How a noisy service is contained.
A rough cost estimate, with what drives it.
